inspiration: Dialogue as a plain, line-based script: spoken lines, options and game commands in one readable file. For us the idea is an NPC script that writers edit without code; keep the structure, write our own syntax.

Once-only and visited gates. A block or option can show a different branch after its first play (Tests/TestCases/Once.yarn). Recreate as a per-character flag on the one ledger, so an NPC remembers a duel or a quest step.

Conditional options that appear or hide by state, and options that vanish after one use (Once.yarn option lines). Good for a gated choice list in the phone UI; the hidden-vs-locked choice is ours to make.
Declared, derived variables: a value computed from other state and re-evaluated on use (Tests/TestCases/SmartVariables.yarn line 9). Maps to derived stats or gate checks in the engine.

Shadow line IDs: one canonical line and a second entry that points at its key, so the text is stored once for every variant (Tests/TestCases/ShadowLines.yarn; YarnSpinner.Compiler/Visitors/StringTableGeneratorVisitor.cs lines 147-151). A clean localisation pattern for our string tables.
Line groups: a set of lines where the first-meeting line and the later lines are chosen by state (Tests/TestCases/LineGroups.yarn). Useful for one character with several moods.
Generated railroad (syntax) diagrams per grammar rule (Documentation/railroads). A good model for a writer-facing rules page that we draw ourselves.

briefs.label: Remembering greeter (first-visit line, later-visit line)
briefs.why: An NPC who reacts to a player who has been before makes a zone feel attentive. Cheap state, big effect. Readable at 375 wide because it is one text bubble, not art.
briefs.keep: A first-time line and a later-time branch on the same node, selected by one stored flag. Signature sound: a short stinger when the greeting changes.
briefs.change: Gate on the duel record (won or lost a fight with this NPC) rather than a plain visit. Give the later line a different voice and a fixed portrait tint. Store the flag on our one character ledger, not in the script.
briefs.ref: Tests/TestCases/Once.yarn and Tests/TestCases/LineGroups.yarn (paths only; this donor is class C, so the idea is recreated from scratch)

briefs.label: Gated choice list (some options appear only when state allows)
briefs.why: Choices that appear or vanish keep a conversation short and make the world feel like it remembers. The option list is the same UI at phone width.
briefs.keep: Option lines with a condition; an option that can be used once and then disappears. Signature effect: the option row fades out after use.
briefs.change: Show a locked row with a short reason instead of hiding it, and draw the lock with our own icon. Make the state source our ledger, not script variables.

briefs.label: Shadow-keyed variant line
briefs.why: One canonical line serves every variant and every language, so writers do not copy text. Costs nothing at runtime.
briefs.keep: A second entry that carries no text of its own and points at the first entry's key.
briefs.change: Use our own plain key scheme and keep the source line next to the variant for review. Do not copy the tag syntax.
